s.d: εὐαρεστέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ hith., [[genesis 5 22|Gen.5:22, 24]], [[psalms 26 2|Psa.26:2 56:13]], al., Sir.44:16 ;] to be well pleasing: τ. θεῷ (LXX, ll. with), [[hebrews 11 5|Heb.11:5-6.]] Pass., to be well pleased: with dative, [[hebrews 13 16|Heb.13:16.]]† (AS)

εὐ-άρεστος, -ον [in LXX: Wis.4:10 9:10 * ;] well-pleasing, acceptable: [[romans 12 2|Rom.12:2;]] with dative of person(s), [[romans 12 1|Rom.12:1 14:16]], [[2-corinthians 5 9|2Co.5:9]], [[ephesians 5 10|Eph.5:10]], [[philippians 4 18|Php.4:18]]; id. before ἐν, [[titus 2 9|Tit.2:9]] (κυρίῳ), [[colossians 3 20|Col.3:20;]] ἐνώπιον, [[hebrews 13 21|Heb.13:21]] (for ex. in Inser., see Deiss., BS, 215).† (AS)
εὐ-αρέοτως adv., acceptably: τ, θεῷ, [[hebrews 12 28|Heb.12:28.]]† (AS)
Εὔβουλος, -ου, ὁ. Eubulus, a Christian: [[2-timothy 4 21|2Ti.4:21.]]† (AS)

εὐγενής, -ές (εὖ, γένος), [in LXX: [[job 1 3|Job.1:3]] (גָּדוֹל), 2Ma.10:13 R, 4Ma.6:5 4Mac 9:13 4Mac 9:23 4Mac 9:27 4Mac 10:3 4Mac 10:15 * ;] 1. well born, of noble race: [[luke 19 12|Luk.19:12]], [[1-corinthians 1 26|1Co.1:26]]. 2. noble-minded: compar., -έστερος, [[acts 17 11|Act.17:11.]]† (AS)
εὐδία, -ας, ἡ (εὔδιος, calm) [in LXX: Sir.3:15 * ;] fair weather: [[matthew 16 2|Mat.16:2]] (Rec., R, txt.).† (AS)

εὐ-δοκέω, -ῶ (on the derivation, see EL, § 28, 6) [in LXX chiefly for רָצָה, also for אָבָה, חָפֵץ, etc. ;] 1. with inf. (Polyb., al.), to be well pleased, to think it good, to give consent (so frequently in π. in legal docu­ments; Milligan, Th., 22 f.): [[luke 12 32|Luk.12:32]], [[romans 15 26|Rom.15:26-27]], [[1-corinthians 1 21|1Co.1:21]], [[galatians 1 15|Gal.1:15]], [[colossians 1 19|Col.1:19]], R, mg. (ICC, in l, but see infr.), [[1-thessalonians 2 8|1Th.2:8 3:1]]; μᾶλλον εὐ., [[2-corinthians 5 8|2Co.5:8;]] with accusative and inf. (Polyb., i, 8, 4), Col, l.with, R, txt. (Lft., in l). 2. to be well pleased or take pleasure with or in a person or thing; (a) with dative (Polyb., al.; 1Ma.1:43, I [[esther 4 39|Est.4:39]]): [[2-thessalonians 2 12|2Th.2:12]]; (b) as frequently in LXX, α with accusative: [[matthew 12 13|Mat.12:13]], [[hebrews 10 5|Heb.10:5]], 8" (LXX) ; β before ἐν (cf. Heb. בּ רָצָה, [[psalms 149 4|Psa.149:4]]): [[matthew 3 17|Mat.3:17 17:5]], [[mark 1 11|Mrk.1:11]], [[luke 3 22|Luk.3:22]] (on the tense, see M, Pr., 134 f.; DCG, i,308 b), [[1-corinthians 10 5|1Co.10:5]], [[2-corinthians 12 10|2Co.12:10]], [[hebrews 10 38|Heb.10:38]]" (LXX) ; (with) before εἰς: [[2-peter 1 17|2Pe.1:17.]] (cf. συν-ευδοκέω, and see Cremer, 213 f.; Field, Notes, 48 f.; DCG, i, 355a.)† (AS)

εὐδοκία, -ας, ἡ (εὐδοκέω, which see), [in LXX: [[psalms 5 12|Psa.5:12]], al. (רָצוֹן), frequently in Sir; in Inscr. (I.G., 5960), LXX, and NT = εὐδόκησις (Died.) ;] good pleasure, good-will, satisfaction, approval: [[matthew 11 26|Mat.11:26]], [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21]], [[romans 10 1|Rom.10:1]], [[ephesians 1 5|Eph.1:5]], 9, [[philippians 1 15|Php.1:15 2:13]]; with genitive obj., [[2-thessalonians 1 11|2Th.1:11]] (see Milligan, in l); ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία, Rec., R, mg., WH, mg. (see Field, Notes, 48 f.), [[luke 2 14|Luk.2:14;]] -ας, Lk, l.with, R, txt., WH, txt. (see ICC, in l; WH, App., in l).† (AS)

εὐεργεσία, -ας, ἡ (εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: [[psalms 78 11|Psa.78:11]] (עֲלִילָה), Wis.16:11, 24, 2Ma.6:13 2Mac 9:26, 4Ma.8:17 * ;] a good deed, kindness, benefit: [[1-timothy 6 2|1Ti.6:2;]] with genitive of person(s) (εὐ. πόλεως, Plat., leg., 805b), [[acts 4 9|Act.4:9]],† (AS)
εὐεργετέω, -ῶ (εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: [[psalms 13 6|Psa.13:6]] (גָּמַל), Wis.3:5, al. ;] to do good, bestow benefit: [[acts 10 33|Act.10:33.]]† (AS)
εὐεργέτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: [[esther 8 13|Est.8:13]], Wis.19:14, 2Ma.4:2, 3Ma.3:19 3Mac 6:24 * ;] a benefactor: [[luke 22 25|Luk.22:25]] (for contemp. usage, see Deiss., LAE, 248).† (AS)

εὔ-θετος, -ον (τίθημι), [in LXX: [[psalms 32 6|Psa.32:6]] (מָצָא), From Th Sus 1:15* ;] ready for use, fit: of things, with dative, [[hebrews 6 7|Heb.6:7;]] before εἰς, [[luke 14 35|Luk.14:35;]] of persons, with dative, [[luke 9 62|Luk.9:62]] (for rabbinic parallels, see Dalman, Words, 119 f.).† (AS)

εὐθέως adv. (εὐθύς), [in LXX: [[job 5 3|Job.5:3]] (פִּתְאוֹם), Wis.5:12, 1Ma.11:12, al. ;] straightway, at once, directly: [[galatians 1 16|Gal.1:16]], [[james 1 24|Jas.1:24]], 3Jn.14 (cf. Dalman, Words, 28 f.), [[revelation 4 2|Rev.4:2]], and frequently in Mt, Lk, Jo, Ac (in Mk, εὐθύς), which see) (AS)
εὐθυδρομέω, -ῶ of ships, to run a straight course (Philo): [[acts 16 11|Act.16:11 21:1]].† (AS)

εὐθυμέω, -ῶ (ὔθυμος), [in Sm.: [[psalms 32 11|Psa.32:11]], [[proverbs 15 15|Pro.15:15]] * ;] 1. trans., to make cheerful (Æsch.). 2. Intrans. (Eur., Plut.; so mid. in Xen., Plat.), to be of good cheer: [[acts 27 22|Act.27:22, 25]], [[james 5 13|Jas.5:13]].† (AS)
εὔ-θυμος, -ον [in LXX: 2Ma.11:26 * ;] 1. kind (Hom.). 2. of good cheer (Æsch., al.): [[acts 27 36|Act.27:36.]]† (AS)

εὐθύνω (εὐθύς), [in LXX: [[numbers 22 23|Num.22:23]], [[joshua 24 23|Jos.24:23]] (נָטָה hi.), [[judges 14 7|Jdg.14:7]], [[1-samuel 18 20|1Ki.18:20 18:26]] (יָשַׁר) [[proverbs 20 24|Pro.20:24]], Sir.2:2, 6, al. ;] 1. to direct: [[james 3 4|Jas.3:4.]] 2. to make straight: [[john 1 23|Jhn.1:23]] (LXX, ἑτοιμάσατε).† (AS)

εὐθύς, -εῖα, -ύ [in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁר ;] 1. straight, direct: τρίβοι, [[matthew 3 3|Mat.3:3]], [[mark 1 3|Mrk.1:3]], [[luke 3 4|Luk.3:4]]" (LXX) ; εἰς εὐθειας, (sc. ὁδούς), [[luke 3 5|Luk.3:5;]] εὐ. ὐδός, figuratively, [[acts 13 10|Act.13:10]], [[2-peter 2 15|2Pe.2:15]]; as (Proper name) of a street, [[acts 9 11|Act.9:11.]] 2. In moral sense, straightforward, right: καρδία, [[acts 8 21|Act.8:21]] (cf. [[psalms 7 11|Psa.7:11 32:11]], al.).† εὐθύς, adv., [in LXX (more frequently than εὐθέως) chiefly for יָשַׁר ;] = εὐθέως, straightway, directly: [[matthew 3 16|Mat.3:16 13:20-21 14:27 21:2-3 26:74]], [[luke 6 49|Luk.6:49]], [[john 13 30|Jhn.13:30, 32 19:34]], [[acts 10 16|Act.10:16, 42]] times in Mk.† (AS)
εὐθύτης, -ητος, ἡ (εὐθύς), [in LXX chiefly for יֹשֶׁר, מִישׁוֹר and cognate forms ;] uprightness: [[hebrews 1 8|Heb.1:8]] (LXX).† (AS)

εὐκαιρέω, -ῶ (= cl., εὖ σχολῆς ἔχειν; used by Polyb. and Philo; cf. Rutherford, NPhr. 205; MM, Exp., xiv), to have leisure or opportunity: [[1-corinthians 16 12|1Co.16:12;]] with inf., [[mark 6 31|Mrk.6:31;]] before εἰς, to devote one's leisure to, [[acts 17 21|Act.17:21.]]† (AS)

εὐκαιρία, -ας, ἡ (εὔκαιρος), [in LXX: [[psalms 9 10|Psa.9:10]] (see Soph., Lex., see word) [[psalms 10 1|Psa.10:1 145:15]] (עֵת), Sir.38:24, 1Ma.11:42 * ;] fitting time, opportunity: before ἵνα, [[matthew 26 16|Mat.26:16;]] τοῦ, with inf., [[luke 22 6|Luk.22:6.]]† (AS)

εὔ-καιρος, -ον [in LXX: [[psalms 104 27|Psa.104:27]] (עֵת), 2Ma.14:29 2Mac 15:20-21, 3Ma.4:11 3Mac 5:44 * ;] timely, seasonable, suitable (Cremer, 740): ἡμέρα, [[mark 6 21|Mrk.6:21]] (or empty, as in Byz. and MGr.; see MM, Exp., xiv); βοήθεια, [[hebrews 4 16|Heb.4:16.]]† (AS)
εὐκαίρως adv., [in LXX: Sir.18:22 * ;] seasonably, in season: [[mark 14 11|Mrk.14:11;]] opposite to ἀκ- (Kühner3, iv, 346 d), [[2-timothy 4 2|2Ti.4:2.]]† (AS)

εὔ-κοπος, -ον [in LXX: Sir.22:15, 1Ma.3:18 * ;] with easy labour, easy: compar., -ώτερόν ἐστι, with inf., [[matthew 9 5|Mat.9:5]], [[mark 2 9|Mrk.2:9]], [[luke 5 23|Luk.5:23]]; with accusative and inf., [[matthew 19 24|Mat.19:24]], [[mark 10 25|Mrk.10:25]], [[luke 16 17|Luk.16:17 18:25]] (Polyb.; the adv. -ως occurs in Aristoph., Fr., 615).† (AS)

εὐλάβεια, -ας, ἡ (εὐλαβής), [in LXX: [[jeremiah 22 24|Jer.22:24]] (דְּאָגָה), [[proverbs 28 14|Pro.28:14]], Wis.17:8 * ;] 1. caution, discretion (Soph., Plat., al.). 2. In later Gk. (Diod., Plut., al.), also reverence, godly fear: [[hebrews 5 7|Heb.5:7 12:28]].† (AS)

εὐλαβέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX: [[proverbs 30 5|Pro.30:5]], [[nahum 1 7|Nam.1:7]] (חָסָה), al., for 15 different Heb. words in all; also Sir.7:29 41:3, al. ;] 1. to be cautious, to beware: [[acts 23 10|Act.23:10]] (Rec.; φοβηθείς, WH, RV). 2. to reverence: [[hebrews 11 7|Heb.11:7]] (cf. Cremer, 388).† (AS)

εὐλαβής, -ές (εὖ, λαβεῖν), [in LXX: [[micah 7 2|Mic.7:2]] AB2 (חָסִיד); εὐ. ποιεῖν, [[leviticus 15 31|Lev.15:31]] (נָזַר hi.), Sir.11:7 א2* ;] 1. cautious, circumspect. 2. devout, religious, reverent: [[acts 2 5|Act.2:5 8:2 22:12]]; δίκαιος καὶ εὐ., [[luke 2 25|Luk.2:25.]]† (AS)

εὐλογέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for בָּרַךְ pi. ;] 1. to speak well of, praise (cl.; LXX [[deuteronomy 8 10|Deu.8:10]], al.): τ. θεόν, [[luke 1 64|Luk.1:64 2:28 24:51, 53]] (αἰνοῦντες, T, WH, mg.), [[james 3 9|Jas.3:9;]] absol., to give praise, [[matthew 14 19|Mat.14:19 26:26]] (see Swete on [[mark 14 22|Mrk.14:22]]), [[mark 6 41|Mrk.6:41 14:22]] (see Swete, in l), [[luke 24 30|Luk.24:30]], [[1-corinthians 14 16|1Co.14:16]]. 2. As in LXX (= בָּרַךְ pi.); (a) to bless, invoke blessings on ([[genesis 24 60|Gen.24:60]], [[numbers 23 20|Num.23:20]], al.): absol., [[1-corinthians 4 12|1Co.4:12]], [[1-peter 3 9|1Pe.3:9]]; with accusative of person(s), [[luke 2 34|Luk.2:34 6:28 24:50-51]], [[romans 12 14|Rom.12:14]], [[hebrews 7 1|Heb.7:1, 6-7 11:20-21]]; εὐλογημένος (= בָּרַךְ; see Lft., Notes, 310; DCG, i, 189), blessed, [[matthew 21 9|Mat.21:9 23:39]]" (LXX), [[mark 11 9|Mrk.11:9-10]], [[luke 13 35|Luk.13:35 19:38]]" (LXX), [[john 12 13|Jhn.12:13;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[mark 8 7|Mrk.8:7]], [[luke 9 16|Luk.9:16]], [[1-corinthians 10 16|1Co.10:16]]; (b) with God as subject ([[psalms 44 3|Psa.44:3]], al.), to bless, prosper, bestow blessings on: with accusative of person(s), [[acts 3 26|Act.3:26]], [[galatians 3 9|Gal.3:9]], [[ephesians 1 3|Eph.1:3]] (Lft., Notes, 311), [[hebrews 6 14|Heb.6:14;]] εὐλογημένος, [[luke 1 28|Luk.1:28]] (WH, tit., R, tit., omit) [[luke 1 42|Luk.1:42;]] εὐλογημένοι τ. πατρός (cf. [[isaiah 61 9|Isa.61:9]]), [[matthew 25 34|Mat.25:34]]; pass. [[acts 3 25|Act.3:25]] (cf. ἐν-, κατ-ευλογέω).† SYN.: see: αἰνέω, and cf. DCG, i, 189, 211; Cremer, 766 (AS)

εὐλογητός, -όν (εὐλογέω), [in LXX chiefly for בָּרַךְ ;] blessed; (a) of men ([[genesis 12 2|Gen.12:2]] A, [[deuteronomy 7 14|Deu.7:14]], [[judges 17 2|Jdg.17:2]] B, [[ruth 2 20|Rut.2:20]], [[1-samuel 15 13|1Ki.15:13]]); (b) of God (Lft., Notes, 310 f.), as chiefly in LXX ([[genesis 9 26|Gen.9:26]], [[exodus 17 10|Exo.17:10]], [[psalms 18 46|Psa.18:46]], al.): [[luke 1 68|Luk.1:68]], [[romans 1 25|Rom.1:25 9:5]] (ICC, in l), [[2-corinthians 1 3|2Co.1:3 11:31]], [[ephesians 1 3|Eph.1:3]], [[1-peter 1 3|1Pe.1:3]]; absol., ὁ εὐλογητός (Dalman, Words, 200; JThS, v, 453), [[mark 14 61|Mrk.14:61]] (Cremer, 769).† (AS)

εὐλογία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for בְּרָכָה ;] 1. fair speaking, flattering speech: χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐ., [[romans 16 18|Rom.16:18.]] 2. praise: of God (as in late Inscr.; LS, see word) and Christ, [[revelation 5 12|Rev.5:12-13 7:12]] 3. In LXX and NT: blessing, benediction; (a) the act of blessing: [[1-corinthians 10 16|1Co.10:16]], [[hebrews 12 17|Heb.12:17]], [[james 3 10|Jas.3:10]]; (b) concrete, a blessing: [[romans 15 29|Rom.15:29]], [[2-corinthians 9 5|2Co.9:5-6]], [[galatians 3 14|Gal.3:14]], [[ephesians 1 3|Eph.1:3]], [[hebrews 6 7|Heb.6:7]], [[1-peter 3 9|1Pe.3:9]] (cf. [[deuteronomy 11 26|Deu.11:26]], Sir.7:32, al.).† (AS)
εὐ-μετά-δοτος, -ον (εὖ, μεταδιδωμι), ready to impart: assoc. with κοινωνικός (for the distinction between the two, see Field, Notes, 213; CGT, in l), [[1-timothy 6 18|1Ti.6:18.]]† (AS)
Εὐνίκη (Rec. -νείκη), -ης, Eunice, Timothy's mother: [[2-timothy 1 5|2Ti.1:5.]]† (AS)
εὐ-νοέω, -ῶ (εὔνοος, friendly), [in LXX: [[esther 8 13|Est.8:13]] Bא1, Dan LXX 2:43, 3Ma.7:11 * ;] to be favourable, kindly disposed: with dative, [[matthew 5 25|Mat.5:25.]]† (AS)
εὔνοια, -ας, ἡ (εὔνοος), [in LXX: [[esther 2 23|Est.2:23]], al. ;] goodwill: [[ephesians 6 7|Eph.6:7]] (of slaves; cf. MM, Exp., xiv).† (AS)
εὐνουχίζω (εὐνοῦχος), to make a eunuch of, castrate: pass., [[matthew 19 12|Mat.19:12;]] metaphorically, εὐ. έαυτόν, ib.† (AS)

εὐνοῦχος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. ὁ τὴν εὐνὴν(bed) ἔχων), [in LXX for סָרִיס (perhaps not of necessity an actual eunuch; DB, see word), [[genesis 39 1|Gen.39:1]], al., Wis.3:14, Sir.20:4 30:20 ;] an emasculated man, a eunuch: [[matthew 19 12|Mat.19:12;]] one such holding, as was common, high office, as of chamberlain, at court, [[acts 8 27|Act.8:27, 34-39]]; metaphorically, of one naturally incapacitated for or volun­tarily abstaining from wedlock, [[matthew 19 12|Mat.19:12.]]† (AS)
Εὐοδία (Rec. -ωδία), -ας, ἡ Euodia (not as AV, Euodias), a Christian woman: [[philippians 4 2|Php.4:2.]]† (AS)

εὐ-οδόω, -ῶ (ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for צָלַח hi. ;] to help on one's way (Soph., al.). Pass., to have a prosperous journey; metaphorically (Hdt., al.), to prosper, be prospered, be successful: 3Jn.2, [[romans 1 10|Rom.1:10]], [[1-corinthians 16 2|1Co.16:2]] (on the tense, see M, Pr., 54; ICC, in l).† (AS)
εὐ-πειθής, ές, (εὖ, πείθομαι), [in LXX: 4Ma.12:6 AR* ;] ready to obey, compliant: [[james 3 17|Jas.3:17.]]† (AS)
εὐ-περί-στατος, -ον (εὖ, περιΐστημι), of sins, readily besetting: [[hebrews 12 1|Heb.12:1]] (on form and sense of the word, see Westc., in l).† (AS)
εὐ-ποιία (Rec. -ιΐα), -ας, ἡ 1. beneficence, doing good: [[hebrews 13 16|Heb.13:16.]] 2. a benefit (FlJ, Ant., ii, ll, 2, al.).† (AS)

εὐ-πορέω, -ῶ (εὔτορος, well provided for) [in LXX: [[leviticus 25 26|Lev.25:26, 49]] נָשַׂג hi.), [[leviticus 25 23|Lev.25:23]] (seel.), Wis.10:10 * ;] to prosper, be well off: [[acts 11 29|Act.11:29.]]† (AS)
εὐ-πορία, -ας, ἡ (εὔπορος), [in LXX for חַיִל, [[2-kings 25 10|4Ki.25:10]] A (frequently in Aq.)* ;] 1. facility. 2. plenty, wealth: [[acts 19 25|Act.19:25.]]† (AS)
εὐ-πρέπεια, -ας, ἡ (εὐπρεπής, comely), [in LXX for הָדָר, etc. ;] goodly appearance, comeliness: [[james 1 11|Jas.1:11.]]† (AS)
εὐ-πρόσ-δεκτος, -ον (εὖ, προσδέχομαι) more usual than δέκτος, which see, acceptable: [[romans 15 16|Rom.15:16, 31]], [[2-corinthians 6 2|2Co.6:2 8:12]], [[1-peter 2 5|1Pe.2:5]].† (AS)
εὐ-πρόσ-εδρος, -ον Rec. for εὐπάρεδρος, which see: [[1-corinthians 7 35|1Co.7:35.]]† (AS)

εὐ-προσωπέω, -ῶ (εὐπρόσωπος, fair of face), [in Al.: [[psalms 141 6|Psa.141:6]], seel. for -ίζω* ;] to look well, make a fair show: metaphorically (as in 7.; see Deiss., LAE, 96), [[galatians 6 12|Gal.6:12.]]† (AS)

εὑρίσκω, [in LXX chiefly for מצא, also for נשׂג hi., etc. ;] to find, with or without previous search: absol., opposite to ζητέω, [[matthew 7 7|Mat.7:7]], 8 [[luke 11 9|Luk.11:9, 10]]; with accusative, [[matthew 2 8|Mat.2:8]], [[mark 1 37|Mrk.1:37]], [[acts 13 22|Act.13:22]], [[2-timothy 1 17|2Ti.1:17]], al.; pass., οὐχ εὑ., of disappearance, [[hebrews 11 5|Heb.11:5]], [[revelation 16 20|Rev.16:20]], al.; γῆ κ. τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ἔργα εὑρεθήσεται (for conjectures as to the meaning of this reading, see Mayor, ICC, in l.), [[2-peter 3 10|2Pe.3:10]], WH, R, mg. Metaphorical, to find, find out by inquiry, learn, discover: [[luke 19 48|Luk.19:48]], [[acts 4 21|Act.4:21]]; αἰτίαν, [[john 18 38|Jhn.18:38]], [[acts 13 28|Act.13:28]], al.; pass., [[matthew 1 18|Mat.1:18]], [[luke 17 18|Luk.17:18]], [[romans 7 10|Rom.7:10]], [[1-corinthians 4 2|1Co.4:2]], [[galatians 2 17|Gal.2:17]], [[1-peter 1 7|1Pe.1:7]], [[revelation 5 4|Rev.5:4]], al.; of attaining to the knowledge of God, εὑ. θεόν, [[acts 17 27|Act.17:27;]] pass., [[romans 10 20|Rom.10:20]] (LXX). Mid., to find for oneself, gain, procure, obtain: with accusative of thing(s), λύτρωσιν, [[hebrews 9 12|Heb.9:12;]] act. in same sense (so cl. poets, but not in Attic prose), [[matthew 10 39|Mat.10:39 11:29]], [[luke 1 30|Luk.1:30]], [[acts 7 46|Act.7:46]], [[2-timothy 1 18|2Ti.1:18]], al. (cf. ἀν-ευρίσκω). (AS)

Εὐρ-ακύλων (Rec. εὐροκλύδων, which see), -ωνος (Εὖρος, the East wind, and Lat. Aquilo; Vg., Euroaquilo), the Euraquilo, a N.E. wind (i.e. between Eurus and Aquilo): [[acts 27 14|Act.27:14.]]† εὐρο-κλύδων (G, εὐροκλ-), -ωνος, ὁ (Εὖρος (seel. εὐρύς, broad), κλύδων), Euroclydon (prob. a sailor's corruption of Εὐρακύλων, which see): [[acts 17 14|Act.17:14]], Rec,† (AS)

εὐρύ-χωρος, -ον (εὐρύς, broad + χώρα), [in LXX for רָחַב ni., and cognate forms ([[isaiah 30 23|Isa.30:23]], al.), exc. [[2-chronicles 18 9|2Ch.18:9]] (גֹּרֶן ;) spacious, broad: [[matthew 7 13|Mat.7:13.]]† (AS)
